1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Nf3 dxc4.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Three Knights, Vienna Variation
1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Nf3 dxc4.background: An instance of the variation at the highest level was Fine against Euwe at the AVRO tournament of 1938.

1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Nf3 dxc4 5.e.strategy: Takes the whole centre at once and prepares to win the c4 pawn back with the f1-bishop. White accepts long-term weaknesses in the pawn structure for space and active pieces; Black must strike at the big centre quickly or be squeezed.
1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Nf3 dxc4 5.e.name: Queen's Gambit Accepted

1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Nf3 dxc4 5.B.strategy: Pins the f6-knight to the queen before Black can organise a defence of the c4 pawn. The bishop develops with a purpose and prepares e4; White wants the pawn back and a strong centre, and Black has to deal with the pin first.
1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Nf3 dxc4 5.B.name: Queen's Gambit Accepted

1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Nf3 dxc4 5.e.strategy: The quiet reply: White prepares to retake the pawn with the f1-bishop and keeps a solid centre instead of grabbing space. The game becomes calm and low-risk, but Black has little to worry about and White gives up the large centre it could have built.
1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Nf3 dxc4 5.e.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Vienna Variation, Quiet Variation

1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Nf3 dxc4 5.B.strategy: Breaks the pin at once and prepares to castle. The knight no longer hangs on the queen, so Black keeps the extra pawn for the moment and can answer White's central advance with counterplay against the pawn chain, instead of passively waiting.
